summary: The bill amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to bar discrimination on the basis of national origin or religion when issuing any immigrant or nonimmigrant visa or immigration benefit, and replaces the broad presidential authority in section 212(f) with a narrower version that requires specific factual findings, least-restrictive tailoring, congressional notice and reporting, public disclosure, and judicial review.

scores.thoughts: The bill contains no provisions related to federal spending, appropriations, or budget authority. It focuses exclusively on immigration entry restrictions and nondiscrimination rules.
No tax-related provisions appear in the bill text.
The legislation does not address healthcare policy, coverage, or markets.
No references to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.

The bill directly amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to expand nondiscrimination protections (including religion) to nonimmigrant visas and entry decisions, while substantially limiting presidential authority under INA 212(f) to impose class-based entry suspensions or restrictions. It requires narrow tailoring, congressional notification, judicial review, and reporting on past travel bans. This strongly expands immigration protections and constrains border/entry restrictions.
No content related to reproductive rights or abortion access.
The bill does not address military or defense spending.

No trade, tariffs, or globalization provisions.
No fiscal or debt-related measures.
The bill adds religion to nondiscrimination language but does not address sexual orientation, gender identity, or LGBTQ+ protections.
No foreign aid provisions.
The bill does not address voting rights or election procedures.
No technology, data privacy, or regulatory oversight provisions.
No labor, union, or employment provisions.

The bill explicitly adds 'religion' to the nondiscrimination provision governing immigrant and nonimmigrant visas and entry, preventing religion-based restrictions. This strengthens civil rights protections against discrimination in immigration contexts.
